name: Rollback Strategy Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday rollback strategy work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical rollback strategy tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday rollback strategy work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical rollback strategy tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Re-check edge cases relevant to rollback strategy (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
2. Measure before optimizing any rollback strategy bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. Before starting rollback strategy work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
4. Keep rollback strategy changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
5. Prefer the simplest rollback strategy approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
6. When rollback strategy guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
7. Document any non-obvious rollback strategy decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
8. Validate rollback strategy outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
9. When rollback strategy decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
10. Prefer explicit, readable rollback strategy solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
11. When multiple rollback strategy strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop rollback strategy edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting rollback strategy assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new rollback strategy abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of rollback strategy correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for rollback strategy, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
